problems.prompt: Put the three steps of ESP operation in the correct order:
choices: Corona charging → electric drift → plate collection
Plate collection → corona charging → electric drift
Electric drift → plate collection → corona charging
Corona charging → plate collection → electric drift
problems.explain: Ions from the corona wire first charge the dust; the field then drifts charged particles sideways; they finally stick to a grounded plate.

problems.prompt: In this teaching model (charge q ∝ r², drag ∝ r), are larger particles generally easier or harder to collect?
choices: Easier — charge grows as r² but drag only as r, so drift velocity w ∝ r increases with size
Harder — larger particles always fall out of the field region
No difference — w is independent of r
Harder — larger particles cannot be charged at all
problems.explain: w = qE/(6πμr) with q ∝ r² gives w ∝ r, so bigger particles drift faster and are collected more easily in this model (very fine particles are the hardest to catch).

problems.prompt: As applied voltage increases (with everything else fixed), collection efficiency η ____ (increases/decreases).
problems.explain: Higher voltage raises E, which raises drift velocity w, which raises η = 1 − e^(−wA/Q).

problems.prompt: Using the Deutsch-Anderson equation η = 1 − e^(−wA/Q), find η for w = 0.08 m/s, A = 4 m², Q = 0.5 m³/s.
